Comment: Geyser Genomics pipeline: QC and alignment in parallel from the raw reads, then variant calling scattered by region (a Map over the planned regions) and merged. Every job gets RUN_NAME = the execution name, which the stages write into the run record (app/provenance.py). Per-stage sizes, the run time limit and Batch API retries come from step_functions.tf (#104); the job definition retries infrastructure failures. Rendered by step_functions.tf with templatefile(); tests/test_state_machine_local.py runs this same file in Step Functions Local.

Check_Gate_Profile.Comment: The quality gate's thresholds for this run (#157): gate_profile in the input (the trigger sets it from the upload's S3 metadata gate-profile). None: default. Checked first, so an unknown profile fails the run before any job starts, never falling back to the default silently.

Prepare_Profile_Error.Comment: An unknown gate_profile, in either gate_mode: an operator mistake, like a mistyped GATE_MODE. JsonToString, so any value (even not a string) gives the message.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('gate_profile {} is not one of: default, synthetic, smoke (thresholds in the image, gate/thresholds/)', States.JsonToString($.gate_profile))

Check_Reference_Name.Comment: The reference genome for this run: reference_name in the input (the trigger sets it from the upload's S3 metadata reference, else REFERENCE_NAME or chr20.fa). It must be a plain file name under reference/ (a non-empty string without a slash). Anything else, including what the trigger flags (mates that disagree, a misspelt metadata key, unreadable metadata), fails the run before any job starts.

Prepare_Reference_Missing.Comment: A manual start without reference_name (the trigger always sets one). Its own state, because the Cause in Prepare_Reference_Error can't read a path that isn't there.

Parameters.Cause: The input has no reference_name (a file name under reference/ in the data lake)

Prepare_Reference_Error.Comment: JsonToString, so any value (a list from mates that disagree, an object the trigger flagged, a number) gives the message.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('reference_name {} is not a file name under reference/ (a non-empty string without a slash)', States.JsonToString($.reference_name))

Check_Reference.Comment: The reference must exist before any job starts: a HeadObject on reference/<name> (metadata only, nothing is downloaded). Its indexes may be missing, since align builds them. A missing key is S3.NoSuchKeyException (the role has s3:ListBucket, so S3 answers 404, not 403) and is not retried.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('reference/{} could not be read from ${bucket} ({}). Upload the FASTA there, or name another reference in the upload metadata (reference=<name>)', $.reference_name, $.reference_error.Error)

Run_Setting_Rules.Comment: Per-run size overrides (cost x turnaround grid, docs/figures/cost-surface-grid.md): an optional object overrides in the input, e.g. {"align_vcpu": "2", "align_memory_mb": "4096", "variant_region_window": 17000000}, merged over these Terraform defaults. Uploads never set it, so triggered runs use the defaults. align_sizes: the Fargate vCPU/MiB pairs align may use (step_functions.tf: valid pairs where max(qc, plan) + align fits in fargate_max_vcpus). The genome's parallelism (v1.3, whole numbers): chunk_count (the large route's alignment chunks), align_concurrency (chunks aligned at once), calling_concurrency (calling shards at once, both routes) and merge_threads; their maxima are rendered from the Fargate Spot cap (step_functions.tf), so a run can't ask for more than the cap holds. dv_parts (v1.5): DeepVariant's make_examples as that many CPU part jobs on Fargate before the GPU job (1 = the single GPU job); dv_shards_by_parts[J] is DEEPVARIANT_SHARDS for J parts (J x the part's vCPUs).

Check_Run_Overrides.Comment: Every check below runs before any intrinsic that could fail on the value: an intrinsic that fails in a Pass state ends the run with States.Runtime, which nothing can catch (no record, no notification).

Inspect_Run_Overrides.Comment: JsonToString works on any value, so this is safe for a list, a number or null; only an object goes on to the merge.

Apply_Run_Overrides.Comment: The overrides win over the defaults. Unknown keys: the state machine can't list an object's keys, but the merged object has exactly setting_count comma-separated parts only if overrides adds no key (no valid value contains a comma), so a misspelt key (align_cpu) fails instead of running the default silently.

Inspect_Run_Setting_Values.Comment: Types are known to be safe here. The window as text: tasks.py needs a whole number, and a JSON number with a fraction or exponent (5.0E7) prints with a . or an E.

Set_Run_Settings.Comment: What this run uses (also in the execution's output): align's size, and the window the planner and the merge both get, as the text tasks.py reads. The concurrencies stay numbers (each Map's MaxConcurrencyPath reads them); chunk_count and merge_threads go to commands, as text.

Choose_Start.Comment: from_alignment: true (v2.0, a manual start) skips QC and alignment and calls variants from the sample's existing alignments/<id>.cram, e.g. to re-call a genome with DeepVariant without redoing ~2 h of alignment. Absent or false: the normal routes. Anything else fails before any job, so a typo never re-aligns silently.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('from_alignment {} is not valid: true (call variants from the existing alignments/<id>.cram) or false', States.JsonToString($.from_alignment))

Check_Alignment.Comment: The CRAM align wrote (tasks.keys_for: alignments/<id>.cram) must exist before calling starts: a HeadObject, as Check_Reference. The callers re-index it, so a missing or stale .crai is fine. A missing key is S3.NoSuchKeyException and is not retried.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('from_alignment: alignments/{}.cram could not be read from ${bucket} ({}). Run the sample through alignment first, or start without from_alignment', $.srr_id, $.alignment_error.Error)

Choose_Route.Comment: Big inputs (v1.3): input_bytes in the input (the trigger passes the upload's ContentLength, both mates added up; a manual start may pass it, e.g. to send a small canary down the large route). At or above large_input_bytes (Terraform large_input_gb) the large route: pre-flight, chunked alignment, a streaming merge. Below it, or without it, today's path, unchanged. A value that isn't a non-negative number fails the run before any job.

Check_Large_Aligner.Comment: The large route aligns in chunks with bwa-mem2. giraffe stays chromosome-scale: its haplotype sampling needs the whole sample's k-mer counts, which chunking breaks. So aligner = giraffe (or anything but bwa-mem2) on a large input fails here, before any job, rather than silently aligning with bwa-mem2.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('input_bytes {} is not a size in bytes (a non-negative number)', States.JsonToString($.input_bytes))

States.Format('aligner {} can not align a large input ({} bytes, the large route from {}): the large route aligns in chunks with bwa-mem2 only (giraffe needs the whole sample for haplotype sampling). Leave aligner out, or set bwa-mem2', States.JsonToString($.aligner), $.input_bytes, $.run_rules.large_input_bytes)

Prepare_Run_Overrides_Error.Comment: Invalid overrides fail the run before any job, like an unknown gate_profile: never a silent default. Only JsonToString and plain numbers here, so this Pass can't fail.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('overrides {} are not valid. Allowed keys: align_vcpu and align_memory_mb (strings, one of the Fargate pairs {}), variant_region_window (a whole number from {} to {}), chunk_count ({} to {}), align_concurrency (1 to {}), calling_concurrency (1 to {}), merge_threads (1 to {}) and dv_parts (1 to {}), all whole numbers', States.JsonToString($.overrides), States.JsonToString($.run_rules.align_sizes), $.run_rules.window_min, $.run_rules.window_max, $.run_rules.chunk_count_min, $.run_rules.chunk_count_max, $.run_rules.align_concurrency_max, $.run_rules.calling_concurrency_max, $.run_rules.merge_threads_max, $.run_rules.dv_parts_max)

QC_and_Align.Comment: QC and align read raw_reads/ directly and don't depend on each other; If either fails, Step Functions stops the other and the Catch below handles it. If either fails, Step Functions stops the other and the Catch below handles it.

Choose_Aligner.Comment: aligner in the input (#146): none or bwa-mem2 runs bwa-mem2 in geyser-app as before; giraffe runs vg giraffe in the geyser-giraffe image (giraffe.tf), same command, keys and size. Anything else fails the run: a misspelt aligner must not silently align with bwa-mem2.

Prepare_Giraffe_Command.Comment: Prepare_Align_Command in the giraffe job definition: the align stage's command, job name and size (the run's settings, overrides included), so everything downstream (and the run record's aligner) is unchanged.

Unknown_Aligner.Cause: aligner must be bwa-mem2 or giraffe (or left out for bwa-mem2)

Large_QC_and_Align.Comment: The large route (v1.3, docs/design/genome-scale-app.md): QC on the whole input, alongside the pre-flight (one streaming pass: gzip integrity, read count, chunk_count equal chunks), then the chunks aligned in parallel (align_concurrency at a time) and a streaming merge (markdup, CRAM). The outputs are today's align's, so everything after Choose_Caller is unchanged. Every job runs on the large-disk job definition. Peak vCPU: QC + pre-flight, then QC + align_concurrency chunks, within the Fargate Spot cap (step_functions.tf derives align_concurrency_max from it).

Quality_Control_Large.Comment: Today's QC command on the whole input, with 8 vCPU (fastp takes the job's CPUs) and the large disk.

Preflight.Comment: tasks.py preflight: fails (PreflightFailed, with qc_reports/{id}.preflight.json still written) on a truncated or corrupt gzip, an empty input or mates out of step, before any alignment.

Read_Manifest.Comment: The pre-flight's manifest (its documented key, intermediate/chunks/{id}/{RUN_NAME}/manifest.json), read straight from S3 like Read_Regions and parsed for the Map.

Align_Chunks.Comment: One align_chunk job per manifest chunk (bwa-mem2 | fixmate | sort, no markdup), at most align_concurrency at a time (the run's setting). The chunk's index goes in as text. Legacy Parameters/Iterator syntax, as Call_Variant_Shards (Step Functions Local).

Align_Merge.Comment: tasks.py align_merge: the chunk BAMs merged in place (presigned URLs), markdup, CRAM + .crai (with the CRAM's ETag), flagstat and mosdepth: the same outputs and run-record part as today's align.

Choose_Caller.Comment: caller = deepvariant (set by the trigger from Terraform's default_caller, or in a manual start) runs DeepVariant on the GPU queue; anything else, or no caller, runs bcftools as before (regions planned, called in parallel, merged).

Choose_DeepVariant_Mode.Comment: DeepVariant split mode (v1.5, docs/design/deepvariant-split.md): with dv_parts > 1, make_examples (CPU-only, ~84% of the stage) runs as dv_parts CPU jobs on the Fargate queue, then the GPU job runs call_variants and postprocess_variants on their examples. dv_parts 1 (the default) is the single GPU job, unchanged.

Prepare_Examples_Parts.Comment: The parts 0..J-1 for the Map, J as text for the command, and DEEPVARIANT_SHARDS = J x the part's vCPUs (Terraform's dv_shards_by_parts[J]: Step Functions has no multiply). Every part gets the same N, which the GPU job checks.

Make_Examples_Parts.Comment:
One make_examples part job per part, all at once (dv_parts fits the Fargate Spot cap), on the Fargate queue in the CPU DeepVariant image. Each uploads its examples to intermediate/dv///shard-

/, its manifest last. If any part fails, bcftools calls the sample instead, as when the GPU job fails ($.deepvariant_error records why). Legacy Parameters/Iterator syntax, as Call_Variant_Shards (Step Functions Local).

Prepare_DeepVariant_From_Examples_Comman.Comment: The GPU job on the parts' examples: call_variants and postprocess_variants only; it checks every manifest before any GPU work. The same DeepVariant task (GPU queue, attempt limit, bcftools fallback) as the single job.

DeepVariant.Comment: Linear DeepVariant on the GPU (variants_deepvariant/{id}.vcf.gz). If it fails for any reason, bcftools calls the sample instead (the scatter-gather path), and $.deepvariant_error records why. pangenome-aware runs hang when call_variants runs out of GPU memory (app-deepvariant/README.md), so the attempt has a hard limit: deepvariant_timeout_seconds (v2.0, long enough for a genome's call_variants; the job's own DEEPVARIANT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is 300 s under it, and its idle timeout still catches a hang within 15 minutes).

Prepare_Plan_Command.Comment: Plans the variant-calling regions (tasks.py regions) after QC and align. Its own step, not a Parallel branch: Step Functions Local re-applies a branch's retry interval when sibling branches finish during its back-off, which made the retry tests flaky. The window is the run's ($.run_settings, set before any job), the same one the merge uses.

Read_Regions.Comment: The regions the planner wrote, read straight from S3 (no Lambda) and parsed into a list for the Map.

Call_Variant_Shards.Comment: Scatter: one variants --region job per region, at most calling_concurrency at a time (the run's setting; Terraform's variants_max_concurrency is its default). Each writes intermediate/variant-parts/<id>/<RUN_NAME>/ (expired by #62's lifecycle rule). On a genome each shard reads only its region of the CRAM (the ETag-verified .crai).

Prepare_Gate_Command.Comment: The quality gate (#144) on whichever caller ran. The job runs with GATE_MODE=warn (pinned here, whatever the job definition or the app default says), so a failed verdict never fails the job itself: it stores qc_reports/{id}.gate.json, and the states below decide. Mode is Terraform's gate_mode. The image must have the gate (main from #148 on).

Quality_Gate.Comment: Parses a few small files: seconds of work, so a short attempt limit (the app's own limit for the binary is 300 s).

Read_Gate_Verdict.Comment: The verdict the job stored, read straight from S3 like Read_Regions. A missing or unreadable verdict is a gate problem, not a quality failure.

Gate_Verdict_Readable.Comment: A verdict without a 'verdict' field (not the gate's JSON, or not an object) would make the comparisons below fail the run with States.Runtime and no notification: it is a gate problem instead. Presence tests never throw.

Gate_Decision.Comment: pass: done. fail (with its reasons): the mode decides. Anything else (verdict null: the gate couldn't judge) is a gate problem.

Gate_Failed.Comment: gate_mode = fail: the run fails with the gate's reasons. warn (the default until a handful of real runs pass cleanly, #157): recorded, the run succeeds.

Prepare_Gate_Failure.Comment: The failure path like any failed stage's (Prepare_Run_Close closes the run record as failed, Notify_Failure publishes $.error): here the gate's named reasons.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('{} failed the quality gate: {} (verdict: qc_reports/{}.gate.json)', $.srr_id, States.JsonToString($.gate.verdict.reasons), $.srr_id)

Gate_Problem.Comment: The gate gave no verdict (its job failed, e.g. a bad GATE_CONFIG or an image without the gate; the verdict is missing, unreadable or null). warn: the run succeeds, through Gate_Skipped so it is told apart from a warned verdict. fail: no verdict is no pass.

Parameters.Cause.$: States.Format('The quality gate gave no verdict for {}: see the QualityGate job log and qc_reports/{}.gate.json', $.srr_id, $.srr_id)

Gate_Warned.Comment: gate_mode = warn and the gate failed the sample: recorded (qc_reports/{id}.gate.json, the run record, the job log, this execution's output) and the run still succeeds.

Gate_Skipped.Comment: gate_mode = warn and the gate gave no verdict ($.gate_error or a null verdict says why). The run succeeds, but it was never judged: it doesn't count toward the switch to fail (#157). The QualityGate stage's FailureCount metric shows a failed gate job on the dashboard.

Pipeline_Succeeded.Comment: Every successful run ends here, after the quality gate.

Prepare_Run_Close.Comment: The failure path, before the notification: the run's closing run-record part (#155), so a run whose failing job never wrote its own part (killed, out of memory, timed out, or a step outside the stages) still ends as failed. The Catch output goes in as it is; the app parses the failing stage, reason, exit code and log stream from it when the record is read (provenance._failure_of). Only fields every Catch output has, so this Pass, which can't catch, can't fail.

Close_Run_Record.Comment: Written straight to S3, not by a Batch job: no Fargate start-up on failure, and a retried job's Cause (every attempt's description) can be too big for a command line. Best effort: if this fails, the run still goes on to Notify_Failure with the original $.error.

Notify_Failure.Comment: Even if the SNS publish itself fails, the run must still end as Failed.

Pipeline_Failed.Comment: Terminal state for any failed stage, so a failed run ends as FAILED instead of SUCCEEDED after the notification is sent.
Pipeline_Failed.Cause: A pipeline stage failed. See the SNS failure notification or the execution history for details.
